description: Results of matches: a service with `results` ({ teams: 2, reportHours: 48, board?, levelRange?, cheaterHint?, cheater? } in neblla_update_app({ business: { booking: { <service>: … } } })) makes each of its sessions, once played, a match between side "A" and "B"; and with neblla_update_app({ matches }) each game a room starts is one too (its id room_…, its title the room's name), reported with neblla.room.matches.report; its players say who won with neblla.business.matches.report. When they disagree it is disputed and counts for nothing until the developer settles it. Action "resolve" { match, winner: "A" | "B" | "draw", note? } (also a match nobody agreed on yet; it moves the ELO board of the service now); "annul" { match, note? } (it no longer counts; the board is counted again without it); "declareCheater" { user, note? }: their open disputes go to the other side, what they said in the rest stops counting, they are flagged and, as results.cheater says, blocked from reporting ("block", the default) or banned ("ban"); "clearCheater" { user } withdraws it (what was settled stays). The actions that only look (disputes, player, cheaters) are in neblla_matches_read.

env.description: "pro" (the published app) or "pre" (its test copy: pre's config, on pre's data, its own unless it plays with pro's). Left out: where the app is, its chosen environment (neblla_promote "status": target, "pro" by default). The pre id (_<id>) as appId is the same as env "pre"

match.description: The match: the id of its session

user.description: The user id in the app
